question: In the finite stability model, is the injectivity of the object direction a property of stability theory or an artefact of the injective A2 model? Dropping injectivity, do two non-isomorphic objects share one graded data?
level: External exact finite linear algebra over F_p plus exact rational slopes; no stable semantic operation, no native admission, no Arakelov, metric or mirror construction
domain: All finite-dimensional A2 = (1 -> 2) representations over F_2 and F_3 with dimension pair of total at most four, one canonical representative per isomorphism class (dim V1, dim V2, rank of the arrow), exact rational slopes
quantifiers: Every isomorphism class (d1, d2, r) with 0 <= r <= min(d1, d2) and 1 <= d1 + d2 <= max_total_dim, in both declared fields
Every subspace pair (U1, U2) with phi(U1) subset U2, over every subspace of each finite space
Every stability parameter in the declared sweep, for every object
acceptance: The graded data records two keys: dimension pairs with slopes, and dimension pairs with slopes plus the rank of the piece itself
A collision under the first key is either exhibited with two distinct isomorphism classes and a parameter, or recorded as an exhaustive negative over the declared range
The rank-including key is tested on the same instances, so the loser is identified rather than described
The injective subfamily r = d1 reproduces the earlier experiment: object direction injective, parameter direction a chamber of more than one parameter
Successive quotient slopes are strictly decreasing as exact rationals at every instance
The rank-weighted slope identity sum_i (dim_i/dim E) mu_i == mu(E) holds exactly
The piece rank is the rank of the graded piece F_i / F_(i-1), computed from phi(U1_i) and the previous accumulated subobject, and never from the dimension vector
protected: The earlier contract experiments/hns_stability_chamber_roundtrip/contract.json is frozen and is not rewritten by this investigation
No claim that this finite model is the Harder-Narasimhan theory of vector bundles, Higgs bundles or arithmetic surfaces
No Arakelov, Green's function, Monge-Ampere, mirror symmetry or Calabi-Yau construction is introduced
F_p exactness is not rational exactness; the declared range is finite and no extrapolation is claimed
No native Rust witness, no library admission, no Seal
residual: This decides one question inside a finite model: whether a graded shadow separates isomorphism classes once the arrow may fail to be injective. It decides nothing about characteristic zero, about sheaves, about arithmetic bases, or about metric existence. If a collision is found, what it shows is that the graded data loses the rank, which in the injective model was pinned to the dimension vector; whether that loss corresponds to an extension datum in a richer category is not tested here.
